projects.name: Kalendra Website
projects.tagline: The public site and early-access waitlist for Kalendra, built with hand-made motion.
projects.summary: The marketing site behind getkalendra.com: a single-page React app that explains Kalendra, an AI scheduling assistant, through scripted SVG, CSS and GSAP animation instead of video, and collects early-access sign-ups through a form. It has no router and no backend of its own, and the Privacy Policy and Terms open as in-page dialogs driven by the URL hash.
features: Animated chat demo: bubbles grow from a waveform and type in sequence on a 35-second loop
Capabilities diagram: logo expands and draws curved connectors to Google, Outlook and Zoom icons
Glass-lens ticker over scrolling job titles using an SVG feTurbulence/feDisplacementMap filter
Looping SVG wave-logo hero with continuously scrolling suggestion chips
Early-access waitlist form (email, role, Android/iOS) sent via EmailJS from the browser
highlights: All motion is code (SVG, CSS keyframes, rAF, GSAP): no video or Lottie files; about 334 kB JS (114 kB gzipped) and 33 kB CSS in a clean production build
Distortion lens built from an SVG turbulence + displacement filter, with sizes switched at a 768 px breakpoint
Capabilities connectors are parametric Bezier paths (width, segment lengths, control offsets, scale) so they can be re-tuned without redrawing artwork
Serverless-style form: EmailJS identifiers come from build-time env vars, the form refuses to submit if they are missing and maps network errors to readable messages
projects.relation: Companion to Kalendra AI, the mobile app. Two separate repositories: this one is the website only.

projects.name: Kalendra AI
projects.tagline: A calendar assistant that unifies Google and Outlook calendars and proposes changes you confirm.
projects.summary: A Flutter app that connects Google and Outlook calendars over OAuth and shows them in one day, week, month and schedule view with overlap-aware layout. A typed or voice assistant turns natural-language requests into proposed event and task actions, and nothing is written to a calendar until the person confirms. It is positioned as a scheduling helper, not a general autonomous agent.
features: Unified day, week, month and schedule views across multiple Google and Outlook accounts
Assistant home with typed or voice turns, summary cards and proposed actions
Partial vs full overlap styling with badges, side-by-side day columns and a picker sheet
Preferred and off-hours windows that clip availability suggestions; per-calendar colour and name
Local daily brief notification at a chosen time
highlights: Hard confirmation boundary: create/update pre-fill the normal event editor, deletes and some task actions use an explicit confirm sheet, execution goes through a separate backend path with a confirmed flag
Assistant turns stream over server-sent events; client keeps history in memory and resends it; voice recordings are uploaded then deleted locally
One merged multi-account event list for a sliding month window feeds all calendar tabs through a shared event model
Conflict clusters distinguish partial overlaps (orange) from exact same-slot overlaps (red); widget tests cover conflict layout and the confirm sheet
projects.relation: The mobile app for Kalendra. Kalendra Website is a separate project: the public site and waitlist.

projects.name: Hearthboard
projects.tagline: A split-flap social board for very short messages, in the feed and on your home screen.
projects.summary: Hearthboard (listed on Google Play as Hearth) lets friends send short uppercase board messages that appear in a feed and on a native home-screen widget styled like a split-flap display. It adds friend requests, reactions, board themes and an optional partner board. An Android TV fork pairs with the phone by QR code for ambient living-room display, but that TV build has not been released.
features: Split-flap styled message feed with reactions and archived boards
Native home-screen widgets showing pre-rendered feed-card bitmaps (light/dark)
Friend requests, search, block list, optional partner board
Board themes (some marked PRO) and tiered subscriptions (basic / pro / max)
QR pairing of phone to Android TV (TV app unreleased)
highlights: Launcher widgets via off-screen renders: the same card is rendered at fixed sizes (distinct iOS aspect ratio), light/dark previews uploaded, URLs stored per message and shown by native widget code
Background post queue so compose stays responsive while multi-friend writes and uploads complete
QR TV pairing: TV publishes a short code as QR, signed-in phone claims it, cloud pairing records subscribed by both sides
Serverless Firestore trigger reads recipient preference maps before sending FCM

projects.name: Al Noor
projects.tagline: A web ledger that replaced a construction company's Excel workbook (Construction Ledger ERP).
projects.summary: An accounting tool built around one Main Ledger of payments and receipts, with Head, Item and Merchant drill-downs and bank, cash and card accounts with running balances. Billed, paid and due are shown at every level. It uses JWT sign-in with a read-only viewer role and an audit log, and contains no AI or ML. Screenshots show fictional demo data.
features: Main Ledger with search and filters (date range, site, head, item, merchant, account, direction, unpaid only, needs review), totals and CSV export
Heads > Items > Merchants sub-ledgers each showing billed, paid and due
Bank, cash and card accounts with opening balance and running-balance statement
Setup for sites, heads, items, merchants and accounts with active toggles
JWT sign-in with roles; VIEWER is read-only, audit log on changes
highlights: Integer money: amounts stored as integer minor units (paisa) and converted at the API boundary
Due is derived from billed and paid so it rolls up consistently across every sub-ledger
Server-side cross-field validation in the Worker (direction, amount, account rules)
Drill-down totals come from grouped SQL aggregates instead of per-row lookups

Four product lines, three service areas and certification badges

Weight (kg/lb) and height (cm/ft-in) units switchable independently; values stored in kg and cm
Local-first SQLite with optional Google/Apple sign-in and Firestore backup

projects.name: Smart Transfer
projects.tagline: Android phone-to-phone file transfer over local Wi-Fi with QR/code pairing and a Phone Clone mode.
projects.summary: Smart Transfer moves photos, videos, music, documents, apps and folders from one phone to another. The devices pair over the same Wi-Fi or hotspot via nearby discovery, a QR code or a six-digit code, then transfer directly over plain HTTP on the local network; a Phone Clone path batches categories for new-device setup. Firestore holds pairing metadata only, not the files.
features: Send tab with categories: photos, videos, music, documents, apps, folders
Pairing via nearby LAN discovery, QR scan or six-digit code
Chunked (256 KiB) LAN uploads with byte-offset resume, pause/resume/cancel
Phone Clone: Old Phone / New Phone multi-category batch transfer
Local transfer history; eleven in-app languages

projects.name: Speaker Cleaner
projects.caveat: Plays synthesized tones through the speaker; no claim that any mode removes water or dust or repairs hardware.
projects.tagline: Android utility that plays synthesized tone sequences through the loudspeaker, plus a speaker test.
projects.summary: Speaker Cleaner plays device-synthesized tone sequences (sweeps, steady and pulsed tones, pink noise) through the phone speaker in five modes: Auto Clean, Water Eject, Dust Eject, Manual Clean and Speaker Test. Presets are rendered as a single phase-continuous 16-bit PCM waveform at 44.1 kHz. The README describes the software only and does not claim any mode removes water or dust or repairs hardware.
features: Five modes: Auto Clean (~80 s), Water Eject (~45 s), Dust Eject (~50 s), Manual Clean (30 s), Speaker Test
Manual mode with user-chosen frequency 100 Hz to 2.5 kHz that tracks the slider live
Speaker Test plays reference tones, a sweep and pink noise for left, right and stereo
Premium subscription removes ads; three modes gated behind watch-ad-or-subscribe
Eleven selectable interface languages

projects.name: Tranquil
projects.caveat: The linked Play listing is the Android TV edition; the app is also live on Amazon Fire TV. The App Store listing covers iPhone, iPad and Apple TV.
projects.tagline: Ambient video-and-sound app on five platforms (Mobile, Android TV, Fire TV, Apple TV) from three codebases.
projects.summary: Tranquil offers looping ambient video scenes and sleep sounds for winding down, sleeping or background calm, with 23 video scenes, 6 looping sounds, a sleep timer and five themes. It is engineered as three codebases: a Flutter Mobile app (Android, iOS), a Flutter TV app (Android TV, Fire TV via store flavors) and a native SwiftUI Apple TV app. There are no accounts; purchases are restored from the store.
features: 23 looping video scenes (8 free, 15 premium) and 6 looping sounds (3 free, 3 premium)
Sleep timer with platform-specific end action; favourites, themes, audio-only mode
Remote-first TV UIs with D-pad focus handling on Android TV, Fire TV and Apple TV
Monthly subscription plus 14 one-time unlocks; rewarded ad grants one hour on Mobile
20 languages on Mobile; English on TV apps

projects.name: Truth or Lie TV
projects.tagline: Android TV party game: vote Truth or Lie on statements with the remote D-pad before a timer runs out.
projects.summary: Truth or Lie TV is a hot-seat quiz for a living-room TV: a statement appears for everyone, each player votes Truth or Lie in turn with the remote (Left/Right, Select to lock), and the TV reveals the answer and keeps score. It supports 1 to 6 players, 3-15 rounds and about 3,550 bundled statements across 15 categories. Native Kotlin app with an emphasis on D-pad focus and input engineering.

100 points per correct vote; final standings and on-device all-time leaderboard
Rewarded-ad, per-category or all-categories unlocks

projects.name: Vizboard

projects.summary: A demo dashboard that switches between 15 interactive chart types (line, bar, 3D scatter, heatmap, word cloud, map, gauge, funnel, radar and more) from one sidebar selector. All data is generated synthetic data; a Streamlit front end was run and a parallel Gradio app exists.

projects.name: Volume Booster
projects.caveat: Adjusts digital gain and filtering; it does not raise what the speaker can physically produce.
projects.tagline: Android and iOS audio-tuning app with boost dial, 10-band equalizer, 20 presets and a built-in music player.
projects.summary: Volume Booster combines a 100-200 percent boost dial, a 10-band equalizer with 20 presets, bass boost and virtualizer controls, and a mini music player in a dark-themed app. On Android effects use the platform android.media.audiofx engine behind a foreground service; on iOS they are applied only to the app's own player via AVAudioEngine. projects.name: World Clock TV
projects.tagline: Android TV world clock: remote-driven grid of live city clocks with a ~48,000-place searchable database.
projects.summary: World Clock TV is a living-room world clock for Android TV showing a paged grid of live city clocks (up to 25 city slots) with per-city weather and a detail view. Wall times come from IANA time zone rule data across about 400 zone identifiers, and cities are searched from a bundled SQLite database of about 48,000 places. The whole UI is driven by the remote D-pad.

projects.name: Would You Rather TV
projects.tagline: Pass-the-remote Android TV party game: players vote on two-option questions and the majority scores.
projects.summary: Would You Rather TV is a living-room party game for Android TV: a two-option question appears, each player votes in turn with the remote, and those on the majority side score a point (ties award none). It supports 2 to 6 players, 3-15 rounds, a per-vote timer and 13 categories with about 2,500 distinct questions. Voting is local only; no online statistics exist.
